messages.content: 你能幫我找到紐約有閱讀室和小說區的公共圖書館，然後在洛杉磯有Wi-Fi和有兒童區的公共圖書館，最後在芝加哥有咖啡廳和閱讀室的公共圖書館嗎？

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

It says facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]; So it can be an array? Actually the type shows "Cafe"[] meaning array of Cafe? Wait the union includes "Wi-Fi", "Reading Room", "Fiction", "Children Section", "Cafe"[]. That means facilities can be either a string among those or an array of "Cafe"? That seems odd. Maybe they intended facilities to be an array of strings from that set. But the type says "Cafe"[] which is weird. Possibly a mistake. We'll assume we can pass an array of strings.

We need to find libraries in New York with Reading Room and Fiction. Then in Los Angeles with Wi-Fi and Children Section. Then in Chicago with Cafe and Reading Room.
